messages:
Ashley M.: quick heads-up — after landing the kernel-selector change last night i'm seeing a perf regression on H100 for larger batches. p95 up ~12-18% for batches with >64 requests (longer avg tokens).
Jordan V.: ugh. is this only H100? any kernel fallback logs?
Ashley M.: A100 shows a smaller bump (~6-8%) at similar batch sizes, A10/T4/L4 look ok. Seen when avg seq_len > 1024 and kv-cache hit rate drops below ~85%.
Priya S.: can you paste the profiling snippet? kernel times / nvprof flame or perf traces would help.
Ashley M.: pasted short profile below (trimmed):
```
H100 | batch_tokens=200k | p50=42ms p95=190ms  (was 165ms before)
A100 | batch_tokens=200k | p50=48ms p95=210ms  (was 198ms before)
A10  | batch_tokens=80k  | p50=95ms p95=420ms  (no change)
T4   | batch_tokens=40k  | p50=118ms p95=520ms (no change)
```
Kernel selector log: falling back from quant-llama-opt -> float32-matmul for some layers when seq_len padded > 1024. That increases memory pressure and triggers more KV eviction churn.
Lee: interesting — kernel selector probably chooses a safer path for H100 when it detects padding patterns. That fallback could be causing extra memcpy + launch overhead.
Mike R.: kv-cache churn: if we evict and refill mid-batch, we pay cold starts per request. Might explain p95 skew. Do we have per-request kv hit traces?
Ashley M.: yes, perf-bot produced KV-hit-rate traces. attaching summary: H100 sessions with mixed short and long requests see cache hit drops to 72% during bursts.
Perf-bot: KV cache hit-rate summary (last 4h): H100 median 88% (burst windows down to 68%), A100 median 91%, A10/T4 medians 95%+.
Jordan V.: proposed mitigation: tighten max_tokens_per_batch per GPU and reduce max_concurrent_batch_size for H100/A100 to avoid hitting the kernel fallback threshold and reduce kv eviction. Also consider per-gpu kernel preference override for quant path.
Priya S.: Agreed. Let's sketch conservative token budgets for a canary sweep (proposal):
```
# proposal: max_tokens_per_batch (tokens summed across requests)
H100:  48000
A100:  36000
A10:   20000
L4:    16000
T4:    12000
# and max_concurrent_batches (cap simultaneous batches to reduce KV churn):
H100: 4
A100: 6
A10: 8
L4:  6
T4:  4
```
Lee: these are intentionally conservative. We should also try an adaptive heuristic: token_budget_target = max_tokens_per_batch * (1 - kv_eviction_penalty), where kv_eviction_penalty = min(0.25, (1 - kv_hit_rate)). That nudges the runtime down during low KV hit periods.
Mike R.: +1. Also add kernel-selector override flag: prefer_quant_path=true for H100 canary to force measured behavior and compare. We'll need to ensure no OOM.
Ashley M.: i ran a quick sim on canary cluster (small load) forcing prefer_quant_path and limited tokens_per_batch to 48k on H100. Results: p95 down from 190ms -> 162ms, p50 roughly unchanged. KV hit-rate rose from 72%->86% during the burst.
Jordan V.: nice. next steps:
- run 6h canary sweep across A100/H100/L4 with conservative budgets above
- collect kernel fallback counts, memcpy overhead, kv hit histograms, and p50/p95 latency by batch_tokens bucket
- test adaptive token_budget_target with kv penalty for 12h window
- if stable, roll to staging and then gradual prod rollout with feature flag
Priya S.: I'll own the sweep job + dashboards. scheduling for tomorrow morning 0700 PDT.
Lee: I'll add the kernel override flag + logging (kernel_selector.debug=true) and a small telemetry ping for fallback reasons.
Perf-bot: Created perf-sweeps run: ID perf-sweep-2026-03-18-01 (canary).
Ashley M.: thanks team. keeping this thread for results. if anyone sees related errors (OOM / CUDNN launch failures) ping here immediately. :eyes:
Jordan V.: also add an alert if kv hit-rate < 70% for >2min in canary cluster so we can abort.
Mike R.: noted. will add abort hook.
Ashley M.: action items summarized: Priya -> run sweep + dashboards, Lee -> flag+telemetry, Mike -> abort hook+concurrency cap enforcement, Jordan -> rollout plan. I'll collate findings and open a follow-up thread with numbers.
Priya S.: thanks, will post initial 2h snapshot in this thread once ready. :rocket:
